english.title: Attendant at count communicate identity of person voted for on particular ballot paper
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person attending at the counting of the votes at an election, namely **(..SPECIFY ELECTION..), communicated information obtained at the counting of the votes as to the

(A)_[candidate for whom]_
(B)_[registered political party towards the return of whose candidates]_

a vote was given on a particular ballot paper
english.legislation: Contrary to section 66(2)(b) and (6) of the Representation of the People Act 1983.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being a person attending at the counting of the votes at an election
communicated information obtained at the counting of the votes
as to the candidate for whom a vote or the registered political party towards the return of whose candidates
was given on a particular ballot paper

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Option B relates to an election of the London members of the London Assembly, as per subsection 66(7) of the Act.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and/or a fine.Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex see section 176Note
On the 12th March 2015, the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' Court was removed - as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
